02 · Responsible space governance
The sky is about to light up, all night
Questions no regulator can yet answer
Caps. The sky tolerates ~100,000 satellites. 1.7 million are proposed. Who sets the limit?
Infrared. Data-centre radiators glow all night. No standard exists. Who writes one?
Costs. Lost telescope time, ozone, debris. Who pays for harms no licence prices?
Jurisdiction. One country licenses; everyone shares the sky. Who decides?
FCC-filings scenario, not a forecast · Crowded Orbits, Fading Skies, European Space Policy, ESA, Dec 2026

03 · Distributed computing in space
Three open problems in orbital compute
1 · Where should a model live when every node moves?
Our placement: 2.34× faster decode than unoptimised, 1.33× faster than terrestrial
2 · How does a conversation survive a handover?
Relay the KV cache (~1.2 s*) on fast links; replay the prompt (~2.0 s) when they’re slow
3 · How does a satellite decide alone?
Onboard LLM: ~87% decision accuracy, beating a rule engine (~81%)
Impact: fewer satellites doing more. AI inference in orbit already beats a terrestrial baseline on our testbed.
Maargin ground testbed · Qwen3-8B FP8, 13 ms per link · *projected at 10 Gbps · animation schematic
